story_type: aircraft firefighting drill on a burning mock MV-22 Osprey
hook: They walked straight into the fire around this Osprey.
narration: These Marines walked straight into the flames around a burning Osprey.
It was a mock MV-22, set on fire in a burn pit at Marine Corps Air Station New River, North Carolina.
The pit is built to make an aircraft fire feel real, so the crews know what to do if one ever happens.
Hose teams moved in shoulder to shoulder.
A fuel fire spreads fast, so crews knock down the flames between the aircraft and the way out first.
Some flames climbed higher than the firefighters.
[short pause] Then the crews closed in on the fuselage.
outcome: The Marines put the fire out, and the mock Osprey was left standing in steam.
title: Marines fight a burning Osprey mockup
description:
Marines with Aircraft Rescue and Fire Fighting at Marine Corps Air Station New River, North Carolina, suppress a simulated burning MV-22 Osprey during an aircraft burn training exercise, Sept. 4, 2026.
